main_text.p: fundantur. Phyficus igitur hominem confiderat, quâ corporis naturalis eft fpecies, anima conftans & corpore, tanquam principiis internis, unde affectiones omnes naturales fluunt. Medicus, qua sanitati corporis est restituendus, vel in eâ conservandus. Ethicus, quâ virtutibus moralibus est imbuendus & ad felicitatem moralem evehendus. Iureconsultus, quatenus ab injuriis externis defendendus, Theologus, quâ ad felicitatem supernaturalem perducendus.
main_text.head: Materiale est corpus naturale.
Ἐξήγησις[?]
main_text.p: I. Non inanis est quæstio de subiecto scientiæ, cum, vt alibi, ita in libro de constitutione naturalis scientiæ Zabarella, & cum hoc melior Philosopho-rum pars affirmat, cuiusque scientiæ differentia a proprio subiecto sumatur, & per hoc propria cuiusq; scientiæ natura constituatur, separeturque ab aliis o-mnibus. Sententiæ Philosophorum, de adæquato physices subiecto, fuere plures. Matthias Aquarius in additionibus ad quæst. Ferrariensi in Phys. postquam in scientiæ subiecto duo dixit considerari, materiale nimirum & formale: pro materiali subiicit, alios corpus, alios substantiam, alios ens posuisse: pro formali, alios naturale, alios mobile, alios sensibile. Cum igitur è tri-bus in se multiplicatis nouem resultent, nouem quo-que de subiecto Physicæ resultarunt opiniones, qua-rum singularum autores recenset: Zabarella in lib. de scientiæ naturalis constitut.cap.5.[?] duas alias adiicit:[illegible, ~6 letters]
[Marginal notes at the right edge of the scan are cropped and only partly legible; their text is not reliably readable.]

page.notes: The right margin holds several short notes that are cut off by the scan edge and cannot be read; only one placeholder is given. The Greek heading is read from a small, spaced line and marked [?]. The "5" in "cap.5." is an old-style figure and is uncertain. The "posuisse" is printed as "posuiffe" with long s, and the "substantiam" word is printed with long s, both normalised to plain s. The printed section mark after "naturale." is not transcribed.
